items.text: Can you dig up what people are saying about the new open-source browsing agent that came out of that Berlin hackathon last weekend? I saw a thread on Hacker News comparing it to a couple of commercial tools, but I lost the link. I'm mainly curious whether reviewers think it actually handles multi-step research tasks or just looks good in the demo. Also, if any write-ups mention licensing, that would help.

intent.requested_action: research coverage of an open-source browsing agent

items.text: I need to track a lost parcel from Marrow & Finch Supplies, order MF-77412, shipped on the 14th. The tracking page has been stuck on 'in transit' for six days and their chatbot just loops me back to a FAQ. Could you check whether other customers have posted about the same courier route (it's going from Leeds to Bristol) and whether there's a known backlog? If you find their real support email or a complaints form, note it down for me. I'd rather have facts than another canned apology.

intent.requested_action: find information about a delayed parcel and courier backlog

items.text: For Thursday's board meeting I want a short briefing on how competitors are positioning their AI assistants in the enterprise sales space. Priorities: pricing changes announced this quarter, any notable security incidents, and which vendors are getting the most analyst attention. Keep it to bullet points I can paste into the deck. No need for deep analysis, just the facts with sources. If something looks like a press release dressed up as news, flag it.

intent.requested_action: gather competitor news for a board briefing

items.text:
We're running our internal hackathon in three weeks and I'm responsible for the judging logistics, so I could use some help gathering background.

First, I'd like a couple of examples of how other companies have structured their judging rubrics, ideally ones that weight practical usefulness higher than novelty. Second, our theme this year is 'tools that reduce busywork', and several teams have proposed automated agents that summarise email or reconcile expense reports. Are there any published case studies of similar internal tools actually getting adopted after the event, or do most of them quietly die? A few examples either way would be useful for setting expectations when I present the results to leadership.

Also, if you come across anything about hackathon projects running into privacy review problems, that would be worth knowing before we award prizes. I don't need a full report, just links and a sentence or two on each.

intent.requested_action: find examples of hackathon judging rubrics and case studies

items.text: Quick one: the board pack for Thursday mentions that we're piloting an AI chatbot for investor enquiries. Can you find out whether any listed companies have disclosed something similar in their annual reports or press releases, and how they described the risks? I want to make sure our wording isn't wildly out of step with what's normal. A handful of examples is plenty.

intent.requested_action: find corporate disclosures about AI chatbots for investor enquiries

items.text: The courier says my parcel was 'left with a neighbour' but nobody on my street has it. Can you find out what consumer rights I have in the UK when a parcel is marked delivered but isn't?

intent.requested_action: look up consumer rights for misdelivered parcels

items.text: Remind me what the judging criteria were for last year's hackathon, and whether the automated scoring tool we trialled caused any complaints.

intent.requested_action: find last year's hackathon judging criteria

items.text: I'm putting together the agenda for the March board meeting and one item is whether we should roll out an AI assistant to the customer service team. Before I write anything, could you pull together what's publicly known about similar rollouts at comparable companies: adoption rates, any union or staff pushback, and what happened to headcount? I don't want vendor marketing, so prioritise trade press and union statements over press releases. Two or three solid sources per point would be ideal. If the picture is mixed, say so plainly rather than smoothing it over.

intent.requested_action: research public information on AI assistant rollouts in customer service

items.text: My parcel from Kestrel Outfitters (order 5581902) has been sitting at a depot in Coventry for a week. Could you check if there are reports of delays at that depot and find the escalation contact for the courier, preferably a phone number rather than a web form? I've already tried the chatbot and got nowhere.

intent.requested_action: find depot delay reports and a courier escalation contact

items.text: For the hackathon opening slide, can you grab me the founding year and headquarters of the three sponsors listed on our site?

intent.requested_action: look up basic facts about three sponsors
